citation.title: Pragmatic generative optimization of novel structural lattice metamaterials with machine learning
citation.authors: Anthony P. Garland, Benjamin C. White, Scott C. Jensen, Brad L. Boyce
citation.version_coded: abstract_only. Abstract reconstructed via OpenAlex's open metadata API (api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1016/j.matdes.2021.109632, queried 2026-09-24). The article is Gold OA per OpenAlex, but ScienceDirect returned an HTTP 403 CAPTCHA challenge to anonymous automated access, both at the article page and at the direct '/pdf' URL supplied in the queue file. OpenAlex's two alternate OA locations were checked: OSTI (U.S. DOE, osti.gov/biblio/1768685) is a metadata-only record with no hosted full text (confirmed via the OSTI REST API: no PDF/PURL link, only citation links); DOAJ (doaj.org/article/894b1237550c4c7eaa5cef47d9e45f70) was not further pursued once OSTI proved metadata-only. A companion OSTI 'Conference' record for the same Sandia project (osti.gov/biblio/1841074, report SAND2021-0287C) hosts a full-text PDF via a direct PURL (osti.gov/servlets/purl/1841074) that downloaded successfully, but inspection showed it is a conference PRESENTATION SLIDE DECK by the same authors (bullet points and figures, ~270 characters of text per page), not the journal article's own manuscript text -- it is not used as the coded full text and is noted only informally below. No CAPTCHA or bot check was bypassed at any point.

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (full text inaccessible). From the abstract: a machine-learning approach discovers Pareto-optimal lattice unit cells trading off elastic stiffness (static loading) against wave speed (impact loading), using relatively few (3500) simulation calls; the abstract itself states no classical-method comparison number.
claim.key_phrase: our artificial intelligence approach works with relatively few (3500) simulation calls
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not derivable from the abstract alone: it states only the ML method's own cost ('relatively few (3500) simulation calls'), with no paired classical-method number to form a ratio. The abstract's background sentence ('Design is primarily guided by human intuition or gradient optimization for simple problems') is a qualitative motivation, not a comparison with a run, timed or cited classical result.

notes: Per the coordinator's clarification (received while coding this queue): when no legal full text is reachable, the record stays included rather than being excluded under a full-text exclusion code, with reason 'I-UNCLEAR (no accessible full text)', stratum 'none', and all rule verdicts 'na'/'no full text'. This record follows that convention. included.method_family is left as 'other' (generic) and dim as 'unclear' because the OpenAlex abstract itself names no architecture or dimensionality; physics is coded metamaterial_homogenization because the abstract explicitly concerns lattice-metamaterial unit-cell design for elastic stiffness and wave-speed objectives, matching PROTOCOL Sec. 3's architected-material scope. Informal, non-canonical secondary source (not used for any formal field above, and not verified against the journal article itself): the companion OSTI conference slide deck (osti.gov/biblio/1841074, SAND2021-0287C, same authors and project) describes a genetic-algorithm (NSGA-II) search over a 12x12-pixel unit-cell design space, using a convolutional neural network trained to predict modulus and wave-speed as the GA's fitness function, run for 11 generations with an active-learning loop; it shows a figure comparing 'Design Results vs 15k Random Designs' and reports validation numbers (3270/3249/3250, units unstated in the slide) for quasi-static elasto-plastic validation. If a later pass gains full-text access, this slide deck (and its implied comparison against a large random-design baseline, which could bear on stratum and R1-R4) should be checked against the actual published Materials & Design text before use, since a conference deck can pre-date or diverge from the final journal version. No author named Jun Wang (authors: Anthony P. Garland, Benjamin C. White, Scott C. Jensen, Brad L. Boyce).
